item.text:
**Verdict**
Mixed, leaning slightly positive on funding/priority-setting, but not on a fully depoliticized management model. The government clearly moved money and policy attention toward BISP, education, health, and social protection, but the personnel picture still looked heavily political and personalized.

**Positive**
- [Pakistan: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on Economic Policies with Pakistan for 37-month Extended Fund Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff) | IMF | 2024-07-12 | Claim: the FY25 budget was to increase BISP generosity/coverage, raise education and health spending, and devolve more education, health, and social-protection spending to provinces through a National Fiscal Pact. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`
- [All you need to know about the new faces in PM Shehbaz’s 19-member cabinet](https://www.dawn.com/news/1821005) | Dawn | 2024-03-12 | Claim: Sharif put banker Muhammad Aurangzeb in the finance portfolio, a notable technocratic appointment in a cabinet that otherwise still mixed in political figures. | IDs: `6B.4`
- [PM Shehbaz declares education emergency across country on Int’l Literacy Day](https://www.dawn.com/news/1857702) | Dawn | 2024-09-08 | Claim: Sharif publicly elevated education into a national emergency and called on private and civil organizations to join the government’s effort. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`
- [Message of Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif on World Children’s Day](https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/27169) | Press Information Department, Pakistan | 2024-11-19 | Claim: Sharif tied child welfare to access to quality education, healthcare, and safe conditions, and pointed to Daanish Schools for underprivileged children in remote and underserved areas. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`
- [Government of Pakistan and Asian Development Bank Signed USD 330 Million “Integrated Social Protection Development Program-Additional Financing” Loan](https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/27426) | Press Information Department, Pakistan | 2024-12-14 | Claim: the government and ADB framed the financing as strengthening social safety nets and improving access to education and healthcare for women, adolescent girls, children, and low-income households. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

**Counterevidence**
- [Of old and new faces](https://www.dawn.com/news/1821157) | Dawn | 2024-03-01 | Claim: most cabinet choices were still long-time PML-N/PDM hands, which weakens the idea of a clean technocratic break in how public services were staffed and managed. | IDs: `6B.4`
- [Sharif personally took charge of ECNEC instead of letting finance minister Aurangzeb chair it](https://www.dawn.com/news/1839967) | Dawn | 2024-06-15 | Claim: Sharif retained direct control over a key economic coordination body rather than fully delegating to the technocrat finance minister, suggesting personalized executive management remained strong. | IDs: `6B.4`
- [Pakistan abusive evictions target urban poor](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/28/pakistan-abusive-evictions-target-urban-poor) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-28 | Claim: authorities forcibly evicted low-income residents, shop owners, and street vendors without adequate notice, compensation, or resettlement, which cuts against a welfare-oriented state in practice. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`
- [World Report 2024: Pakistan](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/pakistan) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | Claim: HRW said the government did little to stop early and forced marriage and that women, girls, minority communities, and children remained highly vulnerable. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`
- [HRCP general body calls for consensus on civilian autonomy, climate justice, and land rights](https://hrcp.wittywebsolutions.com/hrcp-general-body-calls-for-consensus-on-civilian-autonomy-climate-justice-and-land-rights-2/) | Human Rights Commission of Pakistan | 2024-11-17 | Claim: HRCP argued the state had prioritized authority over rights and should instead focus on health, education, workers, peasants, and women, which is a strong domestic critique of welfare governance. | IDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

**Search Gap**
- I found strong evidence of social-service funding commitments and some technocratic staffing, but not a 2024 source showing a broad merit-based overhaul of federal health, education, or social-welfare ministries.
- The positive case is mostly program design, budget allocations, and a few technocratic appointments; the negative case is that political families and personalized control still dominated the broader cabinet and delivery environment.
